Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT) — Advanced Weld & Component Inspection

Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT) is an advanced form of ultrasonic testing that uses multi-element array transducers — typically 16 to 128 piezoelectric elements — to electronically steer, focus, and sweep the sound beam through a component, producing real-time cross-sectional imaging without repositioning the probe. PAUT has become the dominant technique for code-required volumetric weld examination in pressure vessels, pipelines, and structural steel, and under ASME Code Case 2235 it can fully replace radiographic testing for pressure vessel welds.

How PAUT Works

Precisely timed delays — focal laws — between element firings steer the combined wavefront to any angle and focus depth in microseconds. Where conventional UT needs separate 45°, 60°, and 70° probe setups, PAUT sweeps the full angular range from one position. Three displays result: the S-scan (sectorial scan) — a fan-shaped weld cross-section, the primary weld inspection view; the B-scan — a side view built as the probe moves; and the C-scan — a plan view used for corrosion mapping and coverage verification. Focal laws are computed from probe, wedge, and material parameters, then validated on calibration reflectors; ASME Section V Article 4 Mandatory Appendix IV requires demonstrated detection of side-drilled holes at quarter, half, and three-quarter depth.

PAUT Techniques

  • Linear scan (E-scan) — fixed angle, electronically stepped aperture; very fast coverage for plate, lamination, and corrosion mapping.
  • Sectorial scan (S-scan) — 40°–70° electronic sweep; the standard weld technique per ASME V App IV and AWS D1.1 Annex K.
  • Total Focusing Method (TFM) — full matrix capture with every-point focusing for maximum resolution on complex geometry, dissimilar metal welds, and austenitic materials.
  • Adaptive scanning — real-time focal law adjustment for nozzles, curved surfaces, and variable thickness.

PAUT vs Conventional UT

AttributePAUTConventional UT
SetupOne position, all anglesMultiple probes repositioned manually
RecordFull encoded digital imagingA-scan only; manual sketches
Defect sizingDepth and height direct from imageAmplitude-drop methods, less accurate
Speed3–5× faster for equivalent coverageSlower, pass by pass
CertificationUT Level II + PAUT endorsement + qualified procedureUT Level II

Conventional UT remains appropriate for simple thickness gauging and small spot checks; for volume weld inspection, complex geometry, or anywhere a permanent record is required, PAUT wins. Versus RT, PAUT removes radiation exclusion zones and permits, delivers immediate results, and detects the planar defects — cracks and lack of fusion — that radiography tends to miss.

Governing Codes & Standards

ASME Section V Article 4 Mandatory Appendix IV (procedure qualification with demonstration blocks and focal-law validation); ASME Section VIII Div 1 (acceptance criteria); ASME Code Case 2235 (PAUT/TOFD in lieu of RT); AWS D1.1 Annex K (structural steel); API 1104 Appendix A (pipeline girth weld PAUT/AUT with zonal discrimination); DNV-RP-C210 (offshore structures); EN ISO 13588 (automated PAUT of welds). Appendix IV procedures are essential-variable controlled — change a variable and re-qualification is required.

Applications, Services & Digital Twin Integration

PAUT serves oil & gas (vessel and piping welds, tank shells, pipeline AUT at 60–120 joints/day), power generation (boiler and HRSG welds, turbine bores), aerospace (composites and titanium under NAS-410), and manufacturing (forgings, austenitic welds). Frequently Asked Questions

What is phased array ultrasonic testing?

An advanced UT technique using a multi-element transducer whose beam is electronically steered and focused via timed focal laws, producing real-time S-scan, B-scan, and C-scan imaging with permanent digital records — replacing multiple manual probe setups with one pass.

What is an S-scan?

A sectorial scan: the fan-shaped image formed by electronically sweeping the beam through a range of angles (typically 40°–70°) from one probe position. Defects appear at their true depth and position in the weld cross-section.

Can PAUT replace radiographic testing?

Yes — ASME Code Case 2235 permits PAUT (with TOFD) in lieu of RT for pressure vessel welds. It removes radiation hazards, gives immediate results, and detects planar defects better.

What ASME code covers PAUT?

ASME Section V, Article 4, Mandatory Appendix IV — plus AWS D1.1 Annex K for structural steel and API 1104 Appendix A for pipelines. Appendix IV requires a qualified written procedure demonstrated on representative mock-up blocks.

What certification do I need for PAUT?

Typically UT Level II with a PAUT endorsement under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or UT Level 2 with PAUT technique under ISO 9712/PCN — plus, for ASME work, a qualified written procedure approved by an ASNT Level III. Atlantis NDT provides both the training and the procedure qualification.

What is TFM?

Total Focusing Method: full matrix capture records every transmit/receive element pair, and reconstruction software focuses the image at every pixel — the highest resolution PAUT technique, ideal for complex geometry and austenitic materials, now entering ASME and AWS codes.
